questions.Question_Text: A bank predicts whether a loan applicant will default. Positive class = Default. What is recall for the positive class?

An online retailer predicts whether a visitor will purchase. Positive class = Purchase. The marketing team says: Missing a customer who would actually purchase is more costly than contacting a customer who ultimately does not purchase. Which of the following statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Recall should be an important consideration.
False negatives deserve particular attention.
Accuracy alone may be insufficient.
Precision has no relevance whatsoever.

questions.Question_Text: A telecom company predicts customer churn. Positive class = Churn. Only 6% of customers actually churn. A model predicts No Churn for every customer. Which conclusion is most reasonable?

Options.Text: The model may have high accuracy but little practical value.
The model must have 94% recall.
The model has successfully solved the churn problem.
The model must have an AUC of 0.94.

questions.Question_Text: A manufacturing model predicts whether a component will fail quality inspection. Positive class = Fail. Predicted probability of failure = 0.73. Classification threshold = 0.50. What classification would normally be produced?

Options.Text: Fail
Pass
Cannot be determined
Regression prediction

questions.Question_Text: A hotel chain predicts whether a booking will be cancelled. Positive class = Cancellation. The classification threshold is reduced from 0.50 to 0.30. Which of the following statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: More bookings will generally be classified as likely cancellations.
Recall may increase.
Precision may decrease.
The underlying model coefficients automatically change.

questions.Question_Text: A pharmaceutical company predicts whether a patient belongs to a high-monitoring-risk group. Positive class = High risk. The medical team says: We would rather investigate some additional low-risk patients than miss a genuinely high-risk patient. Which action is most consistent with this objective?

Options.Text: Lower the classification threshold.
Raise the classification threshold.
Remove the positive class.
Optimise only for accuracy.

questions.Question_Text: Positive class = Customer responds to campaign. Model A: Accuracy 91%, Precision 86%, Recall 44%. Model B: Accuracy 87%, Precision 67%, Recall 72%. The marketing team wants to identify as many genuinely responsive customers as possible. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Model B has higher recall.
Model A has higher precision.
Model A must be selected because its accuracy is higher.
The cost of contacting non-responsive customers should also be considered.

questions.Question_Text: A ROC graph is displayed showing Model B's curve consistently above Model A's curve. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Model B has better discrimination over the displayed range.
ROC-AUC can summarise discrimination across thresholds.
Model B must have higher accuracy at every threshold.
The final operating threshold should still consider business consequences.

questions.Question_Text: A fraud-detection model produces: Positive class = Fraud; Accuracy = 94%; Precision = 91%; Recall = 38%. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: The model may be missing a substantial number of fraudulent transactions.
High accuracy does not eliminate concern about recall.
The model necessarily has poor specificity.
The classification threshold could be investigated.

questions.Question_Text: A logistics company predicts whether a shipment will arrive late. Positive class = Late. Training accuracy = 97%, test accuracy = 81%, training recall = 95%, test recall = 62%. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Overfitting is a possible explanation.
Generalisation is a concern.
Training performance alone is sufficient for deployment.
Unseen-data performance should influence model selection.

questions.Question_Text: A diagnostic model has ROC-AUC = 0.91. At its current threshold, however, precision is relatively low. Positive class = Disease present. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: AUC and precision measure different aspects of performance.
The operating threshold matters.
AUC of 0.91 automatically means the model is ready for deployment.
The consequences of false positives and false negatives should be considered.

questions.Question_Text: A company predicts employee attrition. Positive class = Employee leaves within the next six months. Exit_Interview_Completed is recorded after resignation. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: The feature may create data leakage.
It could make apparent model performance unrealistically high.
Predictor availability at the time of prediction should be examined.
High test accuracy would prove the feature is legitimate.

questions.Question_Text: An online retailer compares two purchase-prediction models. Positive class = Purchase. Model A: Precision 0.81, Recall 0.48. Model B: Precision 0.63, Recall 0.79. The company has enough promotional budget to contact additional customers and is more concerned about missing potential buyers. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Model B identifies a larger proportion of actual purchasers.
Model A is more precise among customers it identifies as purchasers.
Model B should automatically be rejected because its precision is lower.
The business objective favours giving greater attention to recall.

questions.Question_Text: A quality-control model identifies defective products. Positive class = Defective. Confusion matrix: Actual Defective predicted Defective = 95; Actual Defective predicted Good = 5; Actual Good predicted Defective = 20; Actual Good predicted Good = 180. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: The model's recall for defects is very high.
Five defective products were missed.
Every product predicted defective is actually defective.
False positives still occur.

questions.Question_Text: An e-commerce company predicts the value of a customer's next order. MAE = ₹420. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

Options.Text: The average absolute prediction error is approximately ₹420.
Every prediction differs from reality by exactly ₹420.
The model explains 420% of the variation.
42% of predictions are incorrect.

questions.Question_Text: Which metric gives greater emphasis to unusually large prediction errors because the errors are squared?

Options.Text: MAE
RMSE
R²
Adjusted R²

questions.Question_Text: A property-price model produces R² = 0.78 and Test RMSE = ₹6.2 lakh. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: R² is not the percentage of predictions that are correct.
RMSE provides information about prediction error magnitude.
R² = 0.78 guarantees accurate predictions for future properties.
Both R² and prediction-error measures can be useful.

questions.Question_Text: A model predicts that a player will score 18 points. Actual score = 25 points. Using Error = Actual − Predicted, what is the error?

Model A has RMSE 7.2 and MAE 3.8. Model B has RMSE 5.1 and MAE 4.0. The company is particularly concerned about occasional very large forecasting errors. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: RMSE deserves particular attention.
Model B has lower RMSE.
Model A has lower MAE.
Model A must therefore be selected.

questions.Question_Text: A graph of actual versus predicted production volume shows predictions increasingly below the diagonal as production volume increases. What does this suggest?

Options.Text: The model tends to underpredict high production volumes.
The model tends to overpredict high production volumes.
The model predicts high volumes perfectly.
Multicollinearity has been established.

questions.Question_Text: A learning-curve graph shows training error continuing to fall as model complexity increases, while validation error falls initially and then rises substantially. What does this pattern most strongly suggest?

Options.Text: Overfitting as model complexity increases.
Perfect generalisation.
Class imbalance.
Successful clustering.

questions.Question_Text: Ordinary regression has Training RMSE 2.0 and Validation RMSE 8.1. Regularised regression has Training RMSE 3.5 and Validation RMSE 5.4. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Regularisation may have improved generalisation.
Higher training error does not automatically make the regularised model inferior.
Validation performance is important for model selection.
The ordinary model must be selected because its training error is lower.

questions.Question_Text: Two residual plots are displayed. Model A has residuals randomly scattered around zero. Model B has a pronounced curved pattern. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Model A is more consistent with an adequate linear form.
Model B suggests systematic structure remains unexplained.
Model B proves multicollinearity.
A residual pattern can indicate model misspecification.

questions.Question_Text: A marketing-response model produces Model A: Test R² 0.72, Validation RMSE 4.1; Model B: Test R² 0.74, Validation RMSE 4.6. Model B uses five additional predictors. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Model B's higher R² does not automatically make it preferable.
Model A has better validation RMSE.
Additional predictors should be justified by out-of-sample evidence and business value.
Model B must be selected because its R² is higher.

questions.Question_Text: A credit-risk regression model predicts credit-loss amount. Coefficients: Income +0.42; Debt-to-Income Ratio −0.87; Credit Utilisation +0.61. All predictors are measured on their original scales. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Holding other predictors constant, a one-unit increase in Income is associated with a 0.42-unit increase in predicted credit loss.
A coefficient sign indicates the direction of association, conditional on the model.
Coefficient magnitude alone tells us which variable is most important in all circumstances.
Coefficients should be interpreted together with units and scale.

questions.Question_Text: A hotel predicts nightly room demand. Model A: Train RMSE 3.1, Test RMSE 9.2. Model B: Train RMSE 5.2, Test RMSE 6.0. Model C: Train RMSE 6.1, Test RMSE 6.4. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Model B has the lowest test RMSE.
Model A shows a much larger train-test gap than Model B.
Model A should automatically be selected because its training RMSE is lowest.
Test performance is relevant to judging generalisation.

questions.Question_Text: A residual plot shows residuals mostly above zero at low fitted values and mostly below zero at high fitted values. Which interpretation is most reasonable?

Options.Text: The model may systematically overpredict at higher fitted values and underpredict at lower fitted values.
The model has perfect predictions.
The target must be categorical.
Clustering should replace regression automatically.

questions.Question_Text: A retailer has customer data but no predefined customer segments. What is an appropriate initial use of clustering?

Options.Text: Identify groups of customers with similar characteristics.
Predict next month's sales.
Estimate a binary outcome.
Calculate classification accuracy.

questions.Question_Text: In K-means clustering, K represents:

Options.Text: Number of predictors
Number of observations
Number of clusters
Number of iterations

questions.Question_Text: Which statements about K-means are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: It uses distances to assign observations to clusters.
Variable scaling can affect the resulting clusters.
Cluster labels inherently have an order such as first, second and third.
The choice of K matters.

questions.Question_Text: A silhouette plot shows most observations with values close to zero. What does this generally suggest?

Options.Text: Weak separation or substantial overlap.
Perfectly separated clusters.
100% classification accuracy.
The optimal K is automatically zero.

questions.Question_Text: A retailer obtains: K=2 silhouette 0.48; K=3 silhouette 0.71; K=4 silhouette 0.54. Based only on silhouette score, which solution is most attractive?

Options.Text: All are equally attractive.

questions.Question_Text: A logistics dataset contains Distance 5–2,000 km; Number of deliveries 1–50; Driver rating 1–5; Delay 0–300 minutes. K-means is applied without standardisation. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Variables with larger numerical scales may have greater influence on distance.
Standardisation may be appropriate.
Scaling cannot affect K-means results.
Preprocessing should be considered before interpreting the clusters.

questions.Question_Text: Three customer-segmentation plots are shown for K=2, K=3 and K=4, together with silhouette scores. The hotel specifically wants three reasonably separated and commercially interpretable segments. Which evidence should the analyst consider? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Visual separation of the clusters.
Silhouette performance.
Whether the resulting groups have meaningful business profiles.
The fact that K=4 has more clusters.

questions.Question_Text: A hierarchical-clustering dendrogram contains a large vertical gap immediately before four groups would be formed. What does that gap generally indicate?

Options.Text: A relatively large increase in dissimilarity when groups are merged.
Perfect classification accuracy.
Automatic identification of all outliers.
Regression error.

questions.Question_Text: Ward's hierarchical clustering is being used to segment suppliers. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Ward's method seeks to control increases in within-cluster variance during merging.
A dendrogram can help examine possible cluster solutions.
The method predicts supplier failure automatically.
Resulting clusters still require business interpretation.

questions.Question_Text: K=3 has silhouette 0.71 and average cluster size 1,240. K=5 has silhouette 0.66 and average cluster size 744. Management specifically wants five actionable customer segments. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: K=3 has stronger separation according to silhouette.
K=5 should not automatically be rejected solely because its silhouette is lower.
Business interpretability can legitimately influence the choice.
K=5 must be selected simply because management requested five segments.

questions.Question_Text: A scatterplot contains three relatively well-separated clusters and one observation positioned almost exactly midway between two cluster centres. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: The observation may have relatively weak cluster membership.
Its distances to competing cluster centres are relevant.
It is necessarily an outlier.
Visual evidence should be considered alongside quantitative measures.

questions.Question_Text: A consumer-goods company obtains four clusters. Cluster A: High spend, High purchase frequency, High basket size. Cluster B: Low, Low, Low. Cluster C: High, Low, High. Cluster D: Low, High, Low. An analyst says: We have discovered four fundamentally different types of consumers. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: The statement overstates what clustering alone establishes.
The clusters depend on the variables and preprocessing used.
Business meaning needs to be established through interpretation and validation.
Four clusters prove that exactly four natural consumer types exist.

questions.Question_Text: An employee-segmentation analysis is repeated after removing a small proportion of observations. The cluster assignments change substantially between the two analyses. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Cluster stability should be investigated.
The solution may be sensitive to particular observations.
The original solution must therefore be correct.
Robustness analysis could be useful.

questions.Question_Text: A bank's loan model identifies 120 applicants as likely to default. Of these, 90 actually default. What is the model's precision for the positive class?
A streaming company predicts whether a subscriber will cancel. Missing a subscriber who is genuinely going to cancel is considered costly. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Recall is an important metric to consider.
False negatives deserve attention.
Accuracy alone may not reflect the business objective.
Precision becomes mathematically irrelevant.

questions.Question_Text: A fraud model assigns a customer a fraud probability of 0.38. The current classification threshold is 0.40. The threshold is then reduced to 0.30. What happens to this customer's predicted class?

Options.Text: It changes from non-fraud to fraud.
It changes from fraud to non-fraud.
It remains non-fraud.
The model must be retrained.

questions.Question_Text: A disease-screening model produces the following confusion-matrix counts: TP = 84, FN = 16, FP = 24, TN = 176. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: The model correctly identifies 84 positive cases.
Sixteen positive cases are missed.
Every positive prediction is correct.
False positives are present.

questions.Question_Text: Two customer-response models produce the following results: Model A: Precision = 0.82, Recall = 0.55. Model B: Precision = 0.70, Recall = 0.76. The company wants to identify more of the customers who will actually respond. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Model B has higher recall.
Model A has higher precision.
Model B necessarily has higher accuracy.
The business objective makes recall particularly relevant.

questions.Question_Text: A ROC plot compares two retail-response models. Model A has ROC-AUC = 0.79 and Model B has ROC-AUC = 0.86. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Model B has better overall discrimination according to ROC-AUC.
AUC alone specifies the best operating threshold for the business.
Threshold-specific metrics may still need to be examined.
The consequences of false positives and false negatives may matter.

questions.Question_Text: A retailer predicts whether an online order will be returned within 30 days. A candidate predictor, Return_Inspection_Result, is recorded only after the returned item reaches the warehouse. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: The variable may introduce data leakage.
Its use could make test performance appear better than would be achievable at prediction time.
The variable should be assessed against the information available when the prediction is actually made.
A high validation score proves that the variable is appropriate.

questions.Question_Text: A sales-forecasting model has R² = 0.64. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

Options.Text: Approximately 64% of the variation in the target is explained by the model, under the usual R² interpretation.
64% of predictions are exactly correct.
Every prediction has an error of 36%.
The model will be correct for 64% of future observations.

questions.Question_Text: A model predicts monthly electricity demand of 480 units. Actual demand is 450 units. Using Error = Actual − Predicted, what is the error?

Two forecasting models have Model A: MAE = 4.2, RMSE = 9.1 and Model B: MAE = 5.0, RMSE = 6.4. The business is particularly concerned about occasional very large errors. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: RMSE is particularly relevant to the stated concern.
Model B has the lower RMSE.
Model A has the lower MAE.
Model A must therefore be selected.

questions.Question_Text: A demand model has training R² = 0.94 and test R² = 0.61. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: The difference warrants investigation.
Overfitting is one possible explanation.
Training R² alone is sufficient evidence for deployment.
Performance on unseen data is relevant.

questions.Question_Text: A residual plot shows residuals becoming increasingly spread out as fitted values increase. What does this pattern suggest?

Options.Text: The residual variance may not be constant.
The model has perfect predictions.
The target must be categorical.
The model has automatically detected clusters.

questions.Question_Text: Three regression models produce: Model A: Validation RMSE = 5.1, Test RMSE = 5.4; Model B: Validation RMSE = 4.2, Test RMSE = 7.9; Model C: Validation RMSE = 5.6, Test RMSE = 5.8. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Model B's validation performance does not guarantee the best test performance.
Model A has the lowest test RMSE.
Test performance provides evidence about generalisation.
Model B must be selected because its validation RMSE is lowest.

questions.Question_Text: A regression model predicts employee productivity. The coefficient for Training_Hours is +2.4, while the coefficient for Overtime_Hours is −1.1. Other variables are held constant. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: A one-unit increase in Training_Hours is associated with a 2.4-unit increase in predicted productivity, holding other predictors constant.
The negative coefficient for Overtime_Hours indicates a negative conditional association with predicted productivity.
The coefficients alone establish that training causes higher productivity.
The units of the predictors and target matter when interpreting coefficients.

questions.Question_Text: A retailer has customer information but no predefined labels for customer segments. Which task is most naturally suited to clustering?

Options.Text: Discover groups of customers with similar characteristics.
Predict whether a customer will churn.
Predict next month's revenue.
Calculate classification recall.

questions.Question_Text: Which statements about K-means are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: The algorithm assigns observations to clusters based on distance to cluster centres.
Different choices of K can produce different solutions.
Cluster labels such as 1, 2 and 3 represent an inherent ranking.
Feature scaling can affect distance-based clustering.

questions.Question_Text: An analyst calculates within-cluster sum of squares for K = 1 through 6. The decrease is large up to K = 3 and then becomes much smaller. What might the analyst investigate?

Options.Text: K = 3 as a possible candidate solution.
K = 0 as the optimal number of clusters.
Classification accuracy at K = 3.
Regression RMSE at K = 3.

questions.Question_Text: A customer dataset contains Annual_Spend ranging from ₹5,000–₹500,000 and Satisfaction ranging from 1–5. K-means is applied without scaling. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Annual_Spend may have substantial influence on Euclidean distance because of its scale.
Standardisation could change the resulting clusters.
Scaling is irrelevant to distance-based clustering.
The effect of preprocessing should be considered when interpreting the solution.

questions.Question_Text: A customer-segmentation analysis produces the following results: K=2, Inertia=18,400, Silhouette=0.42; K=3, Inertia=10,200, Silhouette=0.56; K=4, Inertia=7,900, Silhouette=0.53; K=5, Inertia=6,800, Silhouette=0.47. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: Inertia decreases as K increases in this example.
The silhouette score is highest at K = 3 among the solutions shown.
The inertia values alone establish that K = 5 is the best solution.
K = 3 could be investigated further because it combines relatively high silhouette with a substantial reduction in inertia.

questions.Question_Text: A customer-segmentation solution produces four clusters. When the analysis is repeated using a different random seed, several observations move between clusters and the cluster profiles change substantially. Which statements are reasonable? Select all that apply.

Options.Text: The stability of the clustering solution deserves investigation.
The solution may be sensitive to initialisation or the data.
The first solution must therefore be the correct one.
Repeated runs and additional validation could help assess robustness.
